chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Asram ibn Hawshab, from Isa ibn Abdullah, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), who said:
The valleys of the Haram (sanctuary) flow into the Hil (unrestricted area), and the valleys of the Hil do not flow into the Haram.

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: The sacred sanctuary, specifically referring to Mecca or Najaf in this context, considered ritually distinct.
key_terms.الْحِلِّ: The unrestricted or ordinary area surrounding the sacred sanctuary.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on water flowing between the Haram and the Hil in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) articulates a hydrological and legal principle distinguishing the sanctity and jurisdiction of the Haram (sanctuary) from the Hil (unrestricted zone). It implies that the spiritual or ritual purity inherent in the Haram does not transfer outward, whereas the general state of the Hil does not contaminate the inner sanctum, reflecting the hierarchical nature of sacred space in Shia jurisprudence. This principle is often cited in discussions regarding the flow of water for ablution (wudu) and the transfer of ritual status across boundaries.
